analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO trades at 133x trailing P/E with a paltry ROE of 9.74% — paying a luxury price for a business barely learning to walk profitably. The OTA model is structurally commoditised and competitively exposed, leaving no margin of safety at this valuation for a value investor.
key_strengths: Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E: 0.04) with INR 81 Cr cash — discipline rare for a tech startup
Asset-light OTA model delivers 81.7% gross margins and FCF finally turned strongly positive at INR 118 Cr in FY25
Revenue scaling rapidly from INR 501 Cr (FY23) to INR 914 Cr (FY25), reflecting India's digitising travel market
key_risks: Valuation is egregious — 133x P/E, 119x EV/EBITDA, FCF yield barely 1.5% — zero margin of safety by any value framework

Earnings quality is fragile: net profit fell from INR 73 Cr (FY24) to INR 60 Cr (FY25) despite 39% revenue growth; FY24 was inflated by INR 39 Cr Other Income (IPO float), stripping that leaves core profitability razor-thin
Intense structural competition — IRCTC directly, MakeMyTrip, EaseMyTrip — with no durable pricing power or switching cost moat
red_flags: No promoter holding disclosed — opacity on insider alignment is unacceptable for a governance-first investor
Net profit declining (73→60 Cr) while revenue grew 39% signals operating leverage is not materialising as the bull case demands
FII concentration at 64.19% with momentum-driven ownership — any sentiment shift creates violent downside in an illiquid mid-cap
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IXIGO is precisely the category of business I stay away from — a young, internet-era company still finding its profitability footing, priced as though the outcome is already decided. ROE of 9.74% is below what I expect even from mediocre traditional businesses; I would not accept this from a company with a 20-year operating history, let alone one that was losing money as recently as FY22. The operating margin of 7.08% is thin and has not expanded meaningfully even as revenue crossed INR 900 Cr. The FY24 net profit of INR 73 Cr — widely cited as a breakout year — was substantially supported by INR 39 Cr of Other Income, likely interest earned on IPO proceeds. Strip that out and the business earned roughly INR 34 Cr. In FY25, Other Income contracted to INR 23 Cr and net profit fell to INR 60 Cr. That is not the trajectory of a compounder; that is a business still searching for its earnings engine.

The balance sheet is clean, I grant that — D/E of 0.04 and growing cash reserves show financial discipline. But a clean balance sheet does not justify 133x earnings when the business model faces IRCTC (which controls train ticket inventory and has its own consumer app), MakeMyTrip (far larger, profitable, and well-capitalised), and EaseMyTrip in a commodity price-comparison market. Travel OTAs earn thin take-rates and must spend continuously on marketing to prevent user attrition — there is no compounding moat here of the kind I found in Hindustan Unilever or VST Industries. OCF was positive in only 3 of the last 5 years. For INR 7,837 Cr of market cap, I expect consistent cash generation, predictable margins, and a business that gets stronger with time — not one celebrating its first few quarters of profitability.
